extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans of Bill Hicks, music researchers looking for album information
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedia-style article summarizing a stand-up comedy/live album — includes an infobox with release/recording metadata, a lead summarizing significance, sections on musical content and legacy, track listings (including alternate/extended versions), personnel, and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infobox metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The album article includes an infobox listing key album metadata: Released, Recorded, Venue, Studio, Genre, Length, Label, Producer, and Chronology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete infobox with fields such as release date, recording dates and venues, studio, genre, total length, label, producer(s), and previous/next titles in chronology to orient the reader quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise lead paragraph summarizing the album (artist, type, release date, context such as posthumous release) and notable claims about the album (for example, the meaning or theme of the title).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should state what the album is, who recorded it, when it was released, and any notable contextual facts (e.g., 'posthumously released in 1997' and the significance of the title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional ratings / Review scores
rubrics_metrics.description: A section (or table) summarizing professional critical reception, including review scores and sources (e.g., AllMusic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a 'Professional ratings' or 'Reception' area listing review sources and their ratings, with citations to the reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical content
rubrics_metrics.description: A section describing musical aspects of the album (e.g., use of background music, production notes, how music was added to enhance mood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss distinctive musical or production choices, origins of the music (when/how it was added), and any relevant quotes or documentary references that explain those choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: A section detailing the album's influence, references in other works, and its place in popular culture (for example, links to other artists referencing the album or its themes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document notable influences and references (with citations), such as other artists' works that echo the album's themes or that directly reference material from the album.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete track listing with track numbers, titles, and lengths; if multiple editions exist, separate listings for each edition (e.g., 'Arizona Bay' and 'Arizona Bay Extended').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each track with its running time and indicate composer credits (e.g., 'All music composed by Bill Hicks'); separate and label alternate/extended editions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: A personnel section naming performers and their roles (e.g., Bill Hicks - guitar, vocals; Kevin Booth - bass, keyboards, percussion, producer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear list of contributors and their specific roles on the album (musical and production credits).

rubrics_metrics.name: References / citations
rubrics_metrics.description: A references section with footnotes and source citations supporting statements in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite reliable sources for factual claims (release dates, recording sessions, quotes, influence claims). Use inline citations and include a references list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and authority control
rubrics_metrics.description: Article includes category tags (e.g., '1997 live albums', 'Stand-up comedy albums') and authority control identifiers where applicable; may include hidden categories indicating maintenance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add appropriate Wikipedia categories and authority control links; address any maintenance categories (e.g., missing alt text for album covers) to improve accessibility and compliance.
